notes: Runs execute against mock_bridge.py, a fake Hue V2 bridge serving 30 lights / 6 rooms / 24 scenes. Every HTTP request is logged to requests.jsonl, so runs are graded on what the caller actually did, not on what it reports.

evals.name: turn-off-all-lights
evals.expected_output: One `set light --all --on false` call. No full-inventory read, and certainly no per-light fan-out. Reports back how many lights were turned off.
expectations: Did not run a full inventory read (`get light --all`) before writing
Used an --all bulk primitive rather than enumerating lights
Reported the outcome to the user in plain language, including how many lights

evals.name: which-lights-are-on
evals.prompt: Is anything still on? Which ones?
evals.expected_output: A `get light --on true` call, and a plain-language list of the lights that are on. Should not pull the whole inventory and filter client-side.
expectations: Used the --on filter rather than listing every light
Did not request the raw view
Named the lights that are on using their human-readable names
Did not act on a truncated list without noticing

evals.name: dim-room-with-exclusion
evals.prompt: Dim the bedroom to 30% and make it a bit warmer, but leave the night light alone.
evals.expected_output: A single `set room --ref bedroom --brightness 30 --mirek <higher> --exclude night-light` call. Warmer means a higher mirek. The night light must not be written to.
expectations: Targeted the bedroom as a room rather than enumerating its lights
Used --exclude to spare the night light
The night light received no PUT
Raised the mirek value (warmer), rather than lowering it
Combined the changes into a single call rather than several
